entities.name: Aryl nitro reduction
observations: The supplied reactant contains Ar-NO2 and the product contains the corresponding Ar-NH2; the heterocycle, carbonyl, sulfonamide, aryl rings, and C-F bonds are retained.
Transformation is chemoselective reduction of an aromatic nitro group to an aniline, not deprotection or rearrangement.

entities.name: H2 PtO2 EtOH
observations: Strongest exact/fuzzy precedent uses hydrogen gas, catalytic platinum oxide (Adams catalyst), and ethanol for the nitro-to-aniline conversion.
Typical operation is ambient-temperature catalytic hydrogenation under low-to-moderate hydrogen pressure until nitro-group consumption, followed by catalyst filtration.

entities.name: Platinum dioxide
observations: PtO2, also called Adams catalyst, is the supported precedent catalyst for this nitro reduction.

entities.name: Hydrogen gas
observations: H2 is the reducing reagent in the strongest reported precedent for converting the aromatic nitro group to an aniline.

entities.name: Ethanol
observations: Ethanol is the solvent reported with H2/PtO2 for the nitro-to-aniline conversion.
